add: **Function Composition** — composing with a rational function can create new vertical asymptotes where the inner function hits an excluded value.
**Range of a Function** — a horizontal asymptote is usually the value the range approaches without reaching, so the two readings of a graph answer each other.
**Functions Families Gallery** — which families carry asymptotes at all: rational, exponential, logarithmic and tangent, and which never do.
**Piecewise Function Builder** — composing with a piecewise function means tracking which branch each input lands in, one piece at a time.
**Function Reflections** — a reflection is composition with $-x$ or multiplication by $-1$, the simplest non-trivial composition there is.
**Function Composition** — the domain of $f \\circ g$ is narrower than the domain of $g$ whenever $g$ can produce a value $f$ rejects.
**Piecewise Function Builder** — the domain of a piecewise function is the union of its branch domains, which the builder shows as you add pieces.
**Function Reflections** — a horizontal reflection mirrors the domain about the origin, while a vertical reflection leaves it untouched.
**Function Symmetry** — even and odd symmetry can only be tested on a domain that is itself symmetric about the origin.
**Tangent Line Visualizer** — a tangent line exists only where the function is defined and smooth, so the domain bounds where you can drag the point.
**Range of a Function** — the range of $f$ is the domain of $f^{-1}$, which is why restricting one forces a restriction on the other.
**Function Symmetry** — an odd function that is one-to-one has an odd inverse, and symmetry about $y = x$ is the defining picture of inversion.
**Tangent Line Visualizer** — the tangent to $f^{-1}$ at a point is the mirror of the tangent to $f$, so its slope is the reciprocal.
**Function Reflections** — reflecting a piecewise function reflects every branch and swaps which side of a boundary each piece occupies.
**Piecewise Function Builder** — the range of a piecewise function is the union of the ranges of its branches, boundary values included.
**Function Reflections** — a vertical reflection flips the range about the $x$-axis, while a horizontal reflection leaves it unchanged.
**Function Symmetry** — an even function reaches the same outputs on both sides of the axis, so its range is decided by half the graph.
**Function Asymptotes** — symmetry carries over to the asymptotes: an odd function's vertical asymptotes come in $\\pm c$ pairs.
**Function Composition** — composing two odd functions gives an odd function, and any composition involving an even function is even.
**Functions Families Gallery** — which families are even, which are odd, and which are neither, compared side by side.
**Domain of a Function** — the tangent point can only be dragged where the function is defined, so the domain fixes the usable interval.
**Piecewise Function Builder** — transforming a piecewise function applies the same $a$, $b$, $h$, $k$ to every branch and moves the boundaries with it.
**Function Symmetry** — a horizontal shift destroys symmetry about the $y$-axis unless the shift is zero, which is why symmetry is tested before transforming.
**Tangent Line Visualizer** — each transformation acts on the tangent line in a predictable way: a vertical stretch by $a$ multiplies every slope by $a$.
**Tangent Line Visualizer** — the tangent line to each base family in the gallery, showing how sharply the slope varies from one family to the next.
